litigation.mdlName: In re: Uber Technologies, Inc., Passenger Sexual Assault Litigation
litigation.court: U.S. District Court, Northern District of California

phase: Bellwether trials under way; two jury verdicts and one pre-trial settlement
phaseDetail: Judge Breyer has sent individual bellwether cases back to the plaintiffs' home federal districts for trial. A Phoenix jury returned an $8.5 million compensatory verdict in February 2026 and a North Carolina jury awarded $5,000 in April 2026; Uber has said it will appeal the first verdict. The third bellwether, a Texas case, settled on confidential terms in early October 2026 after jury selection and before opening statements. No global settlement program has been announced.
defendants: Uber Technologies, Inc. and related Uber entities

settlements.label: No global settlement program announced
settlements.detail: No court-approved global settlement program or public payout schedule was identified in records reviewed October 17, 2026. Uber has resolved some individual cases, including the third federal bellwether, on confidential terms. A jury verdict in one case does not set the value of another claim.
settlements.source: Top Class Actions report on the third bellwether settlement, October 9, 2026
settlements.individualClaims: Individual settlements reported so far are confidential. A jury verdict in one case does not set the value of another claim.

keyDates.label: MDL-3084 created
keyDates.detail: The JPML centralized federal Uber passenger sexual assault cases before Judge Charles R. Breyer in the Northern District of California.
keyDates.source: JPML pending MDL dockets by MDL number, October 1, 2026

keyDates.label: First bellwether verdict: $8.5 million (Phoenix)
keyDates.detail: A federal jury in Phoenix awarded Jaylynn Dean $8.5 million in compensatory damages and no punitive damages after finding the driver was Uber's agent. Uber said it would appeal.

keyDates.label: Second bellwether verdict: $5,000 (North Carolina)
keyDates.detail: After a four-day trial in the Western District of North Carolina, a jury found Uber legally responsible for a 2019 incident and awarded $5,000. Plaintiffs' counsel reported the verdict on April 22.

keyDates.label: Third bellwether settled before opening statements
keyDates.detail: The Texas bellwether (Jane Doe QLF 001, W.D. Tex.) settled on confidential terms after jury selection.

updates.summary: JPML reports 4,916 pending actions in MDL-3084 on October 1, 2026, up 328 from 4,588 on September 1; 5,221 total historical actions are reported separately.
The third federal bellwether, a Texas case known as Jane Doe QLF 001, settled on confidential terms after jury selection and before opening statements.
JPML reports 4,588 pending actions on September 1, 2026, compared with 4,397 on August 3.
A Western District of North Carolina jury found Uber legally responsible in the second bellwether and awarded $5,000.
A Phoenix federal jury awarded $8.5 million in compensatory damages, and no punitive damages, in the first bellwether. Uber said it would appeal.
